question.prompt:
Given \(AB\parallel CD\), point \(E\) lies between \(AB\) and \(CD\). Points \(A\) and \(C\) lie on one side of line \(BD\), and point \(E\) lies on the other side (\(B\) and \(D\) lie on \(AB\) and \(CD\), respectively). If \(\angle ABE=130^\circ\) and \(\angle CDE=110^\circ\), find the measure of \(\angle BED\) in degrees.

[Figure 1](figures/cnm_070_q3_question_en.svg)

solutions.explanation: Through point \(E\), draw \(EF\parallel AB\). Then \(EF\parallel CD\), \(\angle B+\angle BEF=180^\circ\), and \(\angle D+\angle DEF=180^\circ\). Adding the two equations gives \(\angle B+\angle D+\angle BED=360^\circ\), so \(\angle BED=360^\circ-130^\circ-110^\circ=120^\circ\).
solutions.title: Draw a parallel through E

solutions.explanation:
Use \(BD\) as a transversal to find the sum of the two angles of triangle \(BDE\) at \(B\) and \(D\). Let \(\alpha=\angle ABD\) and \(\beta=\angle CDB\). Since \(AB\parallel CD\), these same-side interior angles satisfy \(\alpha+\beta=180^\circ\). Because \(E\) lies between the parallels on the opposite side of \(BD\) from \(A\) and \(C\), ray \(BD\) splits \(\angle ABE\), and ray \(DB\) splits \(\angle CDE\). Hence
\[
\angle EBD+\angle BDE=(130^\circ-\alpha)+(110^\circ-\beta)=60^\circ.
\]
The triangle angle sum gives \(\angle BED=180^\circ-60^\circ=120^\circ\).
solutions.title: Use triangle BDE
